description: The image illustrates a series of five distinct bar chart patterns arranged horizontally side-by-side, representing different structural distributions. There are no formal vertical or horizontal axes with tick marks, numerical scales, or axis labels; instead, each of the five charts rests on a simple, solid black horizontal baseline. The horizontal dimension of each chart contains an unlabeled sequence of four adjacent bins, while the vertical dimension represents an unscaled magnitude. Every chart consists of four contiguous, light green bars with black outlines. The first chart, labeled "Increasing," shows bars that progressively grow taller from left to right, starting with the shortest bar on the far left and ending with the tallest on the far right. The second chart, labeled "Uniform," consists of four bars of identical height. The third chart, labeled "Decreasing," displays bars that progressively shrink in height from left to right, beginning with the tallest bar on the left and ending with the shortest on the right. The fourth chart features a blurred gray rectangle where its text label would normally appear; its bars form a symmetrical central peak, with the two outer bars being the shortest and equal in height, and the two inner bars being the tallest and equal in height. The fifth chart, labeled "Bottleneck," shows a symmetrical U-shape, where the two outer bars are the tallest and equal in height, and the two inner bars are the shortest and equal in height. The bars within each individual chart are ordered specifically to form these distinct geometric profiles, and the only visual alteration is the gray obscuring box over the fourth chart's label.
